children: A former financial advisor has been sentenced to 11 years in prison for orchestrating a $36 million Ponzi scheme that ensnared dozens of victims. Siddharth Jawahar pleaded guilty to three counts of wire fraud in January.

From 2016 through 2023, Jawahar solicited more than $35 million from his victims through an investment company he controlled called Swiftarc Capital. He invested only about $10 million of that money, nearly all of which he eventually concentrated in investments in Philip Morris Pakistan, according to prosecutors.
All told, Jawahar defrauded 64 victims, including Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, according to news reports from the courtroom.

Jawahar, 38, was remanded to federal custody after the court issued its sentence.  He had been confined to the St. Genevieve County Detention Center in Missouri, where his lawyer, Doug Passon, says he had worked to help other inmates "improve their lives."

"Sid Jawahar is a very good man who has made some very serious mistakes and is taking ownership of all of it," Passon says. "He has made every effort from a jail cell in St. Genevieve to recoup restitution for victims and plans to continue to do [so]."

In a sentencing memo, Passon acknowledged the fraud and said that his client had "made a series of terrible choices" that had cost investors dearly, but argued that Jawahar was committed to repaying his victims and asked for a sentence of four years.
Prosecutors say that Jawahar spent much of his investors' money on a lavish lifestyle that included shopping sprees, meals at pricey restaurants, and private jet travel.

When losses began mounting from the money Jawahar did invest in Philip Morris Pakistan, he falsely told investors that they were still making profits, according to the Justice Department. Jawahar attempted to keep the fraud going by making Ponzi-like payments to earlier investors, according to prosecutors, who say that the scam was one of the largest Ponzi schemes to ever come before federal court in the Eastern District of Missouri.
The Department of Homeland Security released a statement saying that Jawahar is an undocumented resident and apparently making reference to Kelce's team and his wife, Taylor Swift.

"Once he completes his sentence, he will be SWIFTly deported from the United States and live the rest of his life in exile," the department says. "DHS remains CHIEFly committed to deporting illegal aliens so that we can prevent such injustices from ever happening again."
In addition to the prison term, Jawahar was ordered to pay $31.35 million in restitution.
